items.content: The coffee had been brewing for some time before anyone thought to drink it. Its smell moved through the kitchen like something alive, curling around the cold edges of the window frame where pale light was just beginning to gather. There was a loneliness to it — not the desperate kind, but the quiet kind, the kind that belongs only to early mornings and empty rooms and the patient, darkening pot that no one yet had come to claim.

items.content: She had not expected it, and yet there it was — the particular silence that arrives before she even parts the curtains, a hush so complete it seems to press against the glass. Overnight, without ceremony or announcement, the world had been remade. The garden, the roof of the old shed, the crooked fence post she had meant to fix since October — all of it smoothed into something patient and clean, as though the snow had come not to bury things, but to forgive them.

items.content: The last miles unraveled beneath her feet like a sentence finally reaching its period. Something loosened in her chest — not relief exactly, but a quiet surrender, the way a held breath dissolves into the cold air. She had carried the distance so long it had become part of her, woven into the ache of her shoulders and the dust pressed into her skin. Now, standing at the threshold, she hardly knew what to do with her empty hands.
